questions.q: What role does a Solution Design Document (SDD) play relative to the individual diagrams covered in Chapter 1?
options: It assembles the diagrams, decisions, and other design pieces into one coherent narrative a reader can follow start to finish
It replaces diagrams entirely, since prose is always clearer than a diagram
It is only used after a project ends, as a historical record
It is identical to an architecture decision record
questions.explain: An SDD ties together the business context, data model, automation, integrations, security model, and key decisions (including embedding or linking the ADRs and diagrams from Chapter 1) into one coherent document.

questions.q: Which SDD section is specifically where a sequence diagram (Lesson 5) would typically be included, per this lesson?
options: Business context and requirements
Assumptions and open items
Integration design — for any integration where exact order and timing matter
Non-functional requirements
questions.explain: The integration design section covers each integration's pattern, direction, and data exchanged, including a sequence diagram for integrations where exact call order and timing matter.

questions.q: Why does this lesson argue that the 'assumptions and open items' section is not optional?
options: Because Salesforce Setup requires it before a design can be deployed

Because stating an assumption or open item plainly gives a future reader a warning before building on an unconfirmed foundation, rather than letting the gap be silently discovered later, often during an incident
Because it is the only section Trailhead grades on the CTA exam
Because every SDD must be exactly the same length regardless of project size
questions.explain: Leaving this section out doesn't make a design more finished — it just delays discovery of an unstated assumption or unresolved question from now, when it's cheap to raise, to later, when it usually isn't.

questions.q: According to this lesson, how should the depth of an SDD's sections scale across different projects?
options: Every SDD must be the same fixed length regardless of the solution's size
Only enterprise programs are allowed to have an SDD at all
Smaller projects should skip the data model and security sections entirely

Depth should scale to the solution's actual complexity and risk — a small tool's SDD may compress sections to a page each, while an enterprise program's SDD may expand each section into its own sub-document
questions.explain: The nine sections form a checklist, but the depth at which each is covered scales with the solution's complexity and risk — not every SDD needs full-length treatment of every section.

questions.q: How does this lesson connect SDD-writing practice to the Salesforce CTA Review Board?
options: It notes that the skills the board evaluates (sound data model, defensible integration approach, credible security design, clear communication) map closely onto SDD sections, so practicing complete, honest SDDs builds the same competence the board evaluates
It claims the CTA exam requires submitting a written SDD as a separate graded deliverable before the board convenes
It states that SDDs are irrelevant to CTA preparation
It claims the Review Board only evaluates diagrams, never written documentation
questions.explain: The skills the Review Board evaluates largely correspond to the sections of a complete SDD, so the habit of assembling an honest, complete SDD on real projects builds toward the same skills the board evaluates.
